sections.overview: Schinia rivulosa is a noctuid moth known as the ragweed flower moth.
sections.identification: Its forewing measures about 11–14 mm and has alternating grey tones separated by narrow white lines.
sections.habitat: Its main range lies in eastern North America, with scattered records in southern Oregon.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on ragweeds (Ambrosia species).
sections.behavior: Adults fly in late summer and early autumn.
sections.reproduction: The regional life-history account documents the host plants of the larvae but gives no detailed account of egg-laying.
sections.ecology: Its larval dependence on ragweeds links the moth to these flowering plants across its range.
sections.conservation: The regional catalogues consulted do not provide a species-wide conservation assessment.
